prior_importants.description: For a merged session, windowStalled measures from the newest `respawn` of any kind (delivered or not) to the newest gate_result `to: merged`. fixRoundFailure, though, applies stalledAtEnd to the newest *delivered* round window it saw open. A retry round rolled back by startFixRound's undoRound still ends in a running->merged kill, and that kill is what gets measured, not the opened window's. If the retry failed before its `respawn` was appended (writeSessionProfile/launchSession throw, or a `pup kill` while the window opens), the measured span runs from round 1's last hook to the rollback. It includes the idle time while the session sat merged, so the next `pup fix` falsely climbs with reason `stall`. If the retry's kickoff was undelivered, the span is the kickoff wait of about 45s, so a real stall of round 1 is dropped.

findings.description: windowStalled's JSDoc says a fix round's kill counts "when that kill came after the newest respawn", but the merged branch bounds the window by the delivered round's respawn (fixRoundWindow.openedAt) and the first running->merged kill before the next fix_round; a later undelivered respawn does not bound it. Reword to e.g. "when that kill ended the delivered round's window".

The merged branch of windowStalled re-derives the window's end with two findIndex scans plus a handedAt comparison, a second walk of the boundaries fixRoundWindow already tracks; returning a `closedAt` index (first running->merged kill before the next fix_round) from fixRoundWindow would reduce this branch to a lookup and keep the window bounds in one place.

The `read` callback parameter on windowFailureOf (with its inline function type) exists for a single alternate caller, fixRoundRoute; exporting windowStalled and having that caller compute fixRoundFailure(events, windowStalled(...)) directly would drop the callback, at the cost of moving listEvents/decodeEvent into the caller.

fixRoundWindow's switch from a for loop to forEach turns the undelivered-kickoff `continue` into a `return` that silently means "skip this event"; `for (const [at, event] of events.entries())` keeps the index and the plain `continue`.

refuted_findings.description: Since adbe20b, the merged branch starts the stall window at `fixRoundWindow(events).openedAt`, which is the round's own kickoff respawn. That ignores a `pup respawn` made during the round. The trigger: a fix round's window stalls, the operator runs `pup respawn` (which already climbs a rung and records `stall`), then `pup kill` ends the respawned window before its first PostToolUse, Stop or Notification hook. The next `pup fix` then measures quiet from the old stalled window's last write to the kill, finds a stall, and climbs a second rung for the same stall. Before adbe20b the window started at the newest respawn of any kind, so this case did not climb. The `ran` events that `windowFailure` scores are already bounded by that `pup respawn`, so the stall bound and the event bound now disagree.
refuted_findings.refutation: `pup respawn` cannot run during an open fix round: relaunchWindow's first call, requireRunning (src/core/session-handoff.service.ts:72-80), throws when currentFixRound(db, sessionId) is defined. The only other place that appends a `respawn` is the round's own kickoff (fix-round.service.ts:944). So between a round's kickoff and its kill back to merged, no second respawn can exist, and openedAt is always the newest respawn.
